evidence.quote: For every fixed $\alpha$ with $\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}<\alpha\le1$, it is NP-hard to approximate Max-Cut within a factor of $\alpha$. This holds for simple unweighted graphs.

exclusions.reason: Worst-case approximation hardness does not provide a measured runtime or workload guarantee.

outputs.exact_statement: For every fixed $\alpha$ with $\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}<\alpha\le1$, it is NP-hard to approximate Max-Cut within a factor of $\alpha$. This holds for simple unweighted graphs.

Fix a rational $t\in(0,1)$ and a constant $0<\varepsilon<(t-B(t))/4$. For graphs equipped with a rational probability distribution on edges, it is NP-hard to distinguish $$\begin{aligned}
 \textnormal{YES:}\quad&\mathop{\mathrm{Val}}\ge\frac{1+t}{2}-\varepsilon,\\
 \textnormal{NO:}\quad&\mathop{\mathrm{Val}}\le\frac{1+B(t)}{2}+\varepsilon,
\end{aligned}$$ where $\mathop{\mathrm{Val}}$ is the maximum cut weight.

Fix $0<t<1$ and $\xi>0$. There are an integer $K\ge1$ and $\tau>0$, depending only on $t,\xi$, such that every $h:\{-1,1\}^\Omega\to[-1,1]$ with $\mathbb Eh=0$ satisfies $$\bigl(\mathop{\mathrm{Inf}}_a^{\le K}(h)<\tau\text{ for all }a\in\Omega\bigr)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathop{\mathrm{Stab}}_t(h)\le B(t)+\xi.$$

For every constant $b\in(0,1)$ there is an integer $n\geq 1$ such that, for every constant $a\in(0,1-b)$, the following promise problem is NP-hard. Its input is a weighted bipartite game with vertex sets $X,Y$, respective label sets $\mathbb F_2^{n+1},\mathbb F_2^n$, and a surjective affine map $$\pi_e:\mathbb F_2^{n+1}\longrightarrow\mathbb F_2^n$$ on each edge $e=(x,y)$. An edge is satisfied when $\pi_e(\lambda_X(x))=\lambda_Y(y)$. The promise cases are $$\mathrm{YES}:\quad \mathop{\mathrm{Val}}(\mathcal G)\geq 1-a,
  \qquad
  \mathrm{NO}:\quad \mathop{\mathrm{Val}}(\mathcal G)\leq b.$$ The integer $n$ depends on $b$ alone. For fixed $a,b$, the reduction is deterministic and has polynomial running time and output size.

For every fixed collection of tables $F$, the root output as a multilinear polynomial in the $k$ leaf signs has only degree-$d$ monomials. Each such monomial chooses one child from every pair at every node that it reaches. Every resulting traversal meets every possible slice $\mathcal D$ at exactly one node. Consequently, negating all the tables on a slice negates $W$.*


*Let $0<t<1$ and $0<r<1$. Draw $F$ uniformly, and construct $F'$ by leaving the tables outside $\mathcal D$ unchanged and coupling each pair of corresponding table entries on $\mathcal D$ as uniform signs of correlation $t$, independently across entries. Independently draw $R\in H^k$ uniformly, and form $R^1,R^2$ by retaining each row of $R$ with probability $r$ and otherwise replacing it by an independent uniform row, independently in the two copies. Then, for every $a\in\mathcal A$ and every fixed slice, $$\mathbb E\bigl[W(R^1,F)(a)W(R^2,F')(a)\mid\mathcal D\bigr]
       =t r^{2d}.
 \label{eq:tree-correlation}$$ In particular, if $r=1-\mu/d$ with $0<\mu<1/2$, then $r^{2d}\ge1-2\mu$.

Let $f$ be a function of the code. Every nonzero row Fourier coefficient of $f$ satisfies, at each internal node $v$, $$q_{v,g0}+q_{v,g1}=q_v\qquad(g\in[s]).
 \label{eq:row-relations}$$ For a table collection $F$, let $F^{v,-}$ negate $F_v$ alone, and let $F^{v,z}$ replace $F_v(u)$ by $F_v(u+z)$, leaving all other tables unchanged. Then $$\begin{aligned}
 \widehat f_C(F^{v,-})
   &=(-1)^{q_v(\mathbf 1)}\widehat f_C(F),
   \label{eq:table-flip-action}\\
 \widehat f_C(F^{v,z})
   &=(-1)^{\sum_g z_g q_{v,g1}(\mathbf 1)}\widehat f_C(F).
   \label{eq:table-translation-action}
\end{aligned}$$ All these statements remain true after row smoothing. They are also preserved by row Fourier projections and by projection to any range of total Fourier degrees in the entries of a specified collection of whole gate tables.

The change of coordinates $$H^k\longrightarrow H^{2s}\times H^{k-2s},\qquad R\longmapsto((L_{g,b}),\Gamma)$$ is a linear bijection. In particular, under uniform rows the free shifts are independent uniforms conditional on $\Gamma$. The Fourier index of $L_{g,b}$ corresponding to a full row index $C$ is $Q_{g,b}=q_{v,g b}$.* *Consequently, at every fixed $\Gamma$, the operator $S_v$ acts as the Fourier projection in the $2s$ shifts onto precisely the unsplit shift indices. For a function of the code or its row smoothing, the shift coefficients vanish unless the sums $Q_{g,0}+Q_{g,1}$ are the same for every $g$. The table actions in Equations [eq:table-flip-action] and [eq:table-translation-action] hold for each shift coefficient at this fixed context, with $q_v=Q_{1,0}+Q_{1,1}$ and $q_{v,g1}=Q_{g,1}$.

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb F_2$, write $\chi_q(u)=(-1)^{q(u)}$ for $q\in H^*$ and $u\in H$, let $\mathcal V$ be a real Hilbert space, let $s\ge1$ be an integer, and let $$c(q,z)\in\mathcal V,
 \qquad q\in H^*,\quad z\in\mathbb F_2^s.$$ Set $$w_q=\sum_{z\in\mathbb F_2^s}\norm{c(q,z)}^2,
 \qquad M=\sum_{q\in H^*}w_q.$$ Choose $L,J_1,\ldots,J_s$ independently and uniformly in $H$, and define $$\mathbf J(q)=(q(J_1),\ldots,q(J_s)),
 \qquad
 U(z)=\sum_{q\in H^*}\chi_q(L)c(q,z+\mathbf J(q)).$$ Then $$\label{eq:hashing-total-mass}
 \mathbb E\sum_{z\in\mathbb F_2^s}\norm{U(z)}^2=M.$$ For every $\zeta>0$, there are $\gamma>0$ and $s_0\in\mathbb N$, depending only on $\zeta$, such that for every $s\ge s_0$, $$\label{eq:hashing-dispersion}
 \max_{q\in H^*}w_q\le\gamma M
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathbb E\max_{z\in\mathbb F_2^s}\norm{U(z)}^2\le\zeta M.$$

Suppose the extraction conclusion of Proposition 13 holds with constants $p_*,\theta>0$. If $T$ satisfies Equation [eq:decoder-repetition], then the original affine game has value at least $$\label{eq:decoded-value} \mathop{\mathrm{Val}}(\mathcal G)\geq 2^{-2s}\frac{p_*\theta}{2}.$$

Let $X$ have dimension $3k_0$, let $H\le X$ have dimension $k_0$, and let $h:H\to\mathbb F_2$ be linear. Suppose a table $F$ assigns a linear function to every $\ell$-space, and that for every $(\ell+k_0)$-space $K\supseteq H$ there is a linear function $f_K:K\to\mathbb F_2$ such that $f_K|_H=h$ and $F[L]=f_K|_L$ whenever $L+H=K$. Fix a $q$-space $Q$ with $Q\cap H=\{0\}$, and set $$e_{k_0}=2^{\ell+r-2k_0+1}.$$ Assume $q\le\ell$, $3k_0-r>\ell$, [eq:affine-validity-ell-margin], and $e_{k_0}\le\tau_0/4$. For $Q\subseteq W\subseteq X$ of codimension $i\le r$, say that $(g,W)$ occurs if $g:W\to\mathbb F_2$ is linear and $$\Pr_{Q\subseteq L\subseteq W,\ \dim L=\ell} [F[L]=g|_L]>\tau_i.$$ Call it maximal if it has no occurring extension to a strictly larger space. Every maximal occurring pair satisfies $H\subseteq W$ and $g|_H=h$.

Let $G$ be a graph on $N$ vertices with nonnegative rational weights $w_{uv}$ on unordered distinct vertex pairs, and $\sum_{u<v}w_{uv}\le1$. For every fixed $\epsilon'>0$, one can construct in deterministic polynomial time a simple unweighted graph $G'$ and an integer scale $Q$ such that $$\left|\frac{\operatorname{MaxCut}(G')}{Q}
             -\operatorname{MaxCut}(G)\right|\le\epsilon'.$$ The same conclusion holds when the input graph has loops, after deleting them without renormalizing its other weights.
